title_en: Commentary on al-Mughnī al-Mufīd — Tape Eight
body_ar: الثانية عشرة جده (ص) بحيث فعل ما نسب بسببه إلى الجنون، فإنه (ص) لما أنزل عليه وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين دعاهم أجمعين حتى اجتمعوا حوله عند الصفا، فلما أخبرهم أنه النذير العريان وأنه نذير لهم بين يدي عذاب شديد، قال له أبو لهب تبا لك ألمثل هذا تجمعنا، فأنزل الله تعالى: ﴿تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب﴾ وكانوا يسألونه أبك جنون لأنهم لم يفهموا دعوته
body_en: Twelfth: his earnestness, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the point that he did what caused him to be charged with madness. For when there was revealed to him {And warn your nearest kinsfolk} (Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:214), he summoned them all until they had gathered around him at al-Safa; and when he told them that he was the naked warner (al-nadhīr al-ʿuryān) and that he was a warner to them of a severe punishment lying ahead of them, Abu Lahab said to him: 'May you perish — is it for something like this that you gather us?' So God, exalted is He, sent down: {Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth availed him nothing, nor what he earned.} (Sūrat al-Masad 111:1–2). And they used to ask him, 'Are you mad?' — because they did not understand his call

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.context: فلما أخبرهم أنه النذير العريان وأنه نذير لهم بين يدي عذاب شديد
options: the scout who strips off his clothes to warn his people
flags.note: A pre-Islamic proverb: the lookout who sees a raiding party, tears off his garment and waves it so his tribe knows the danger is real. The image is opaque in English. Option 1 explains it but supplies an explanation the Sheikh did not give; option 0 keeps his words and leaves the explaining to an editorial note. A reviewer should decide whether the corpus permits such notes.

flags.context: الثانية عشرة جده (ص) بحيث فعل ما نسب بسببه إلى الجنون
options: the urgency with which he acted
flags.note: Unvowelled جده could be read jidduhu ('his earnestness') or jadduhu ('his grandfather' / 'his fortune'). The context — acting so intensely that he was charged with madness — fixes it as jidd. Flagged because the reading is the translator's, not the source's.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.
Q 26:214 is quoted in the Arabic without brackets, run into the sentence; it has been set in curly brackets with its reference per house style.
The excerpt ends without final punctuation, mid-flow.
